name: momentum_exhaustion_vix_reversal
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, a sharp vertical price move (RSI(6) reaching extreme levels in 30 seconds) accompanied by a volume surge >3x the 10-minute baseline while VIX is simultaneously rising signals that directional flow is hitting absorption. Market makers and delta-hedgers who are short gamma from recent option sales begin reversing their hedges within 1-3 bars as the move stalls, creating an immediate mean reversion impulse. The first confirming bar — price ticking in the reversal direction — is the entry trigger; the reversal typically recovers 15-20 NIFTY spot points within 60-90 seconds as systematic stop-orders finish executing and resting limit orders on the other side absorb remaining flow.

indicators.name: rsi_6
indicators.purpose: 30-second RSI (6 bars × 5s) to detect ultra-short-term exhaustion. The original uses RSI(2) on 1-min bars (2-minute sensitivity). At 5s, RSI(6) gives equivalent 30-second sensitivity — fast enough to catch the tail of the exhaustion move while avoiding single-bar noise. NOT scaled by 12x (which would give RSI(24) = 2 minutes, too smooth to be an exhaustion detector); instead kept at 6 bars to preserve the original's 'last few bars are all one direction' property. Thresholds widened to 20/80 because RSI(6) mean-reverts more slowly than RSI(2).

indicators.name: vol_climax
indicators.purpose: 120 bars = 10-minute volume baseline. The original uses SMA(50) on 1-min bars (50-minute context). Compressed to 10 minutes because we need a RECENT baseline — a 50-minute window blends different intraday volatility regimes. The 10-minute window captures the current session's volume rhythm without over-averaging. 3x multiplier preserved from original as the exhaustion threshold.

indicators.name: vix_slope_6
indicators.purpose: VIX rising over the last 30 seconds (6 bars) confirms fear/panic is actively expanding, not just elevated. The original checks vix > prev_vix (single 1-min bar change). At 5s, single-bar VIX changes are too noisy; a 6-bar window (30s) filters micro-fluctuations while still capturing genuine VIX upticks that precede exhaustion reversals.

conditions: rsi_6 < rsi_oversold (default 20) — price has crashed in last 30s
vix_close[i] > vix_close[i-6] — VIX rising over last 30s
close[i] > close[i-1] — first uptick confirming reversal starting
buy_ce.confirmation: Price ticking up on the first bar after extreme RSI oversold + volume climax

conditions: rsi_6 > rsi_overbought (default 80) — price has surged in last 30s
vix_close[i] > vix_close[i-6] — VIX rising over last 30s
close[i] < close[i-1] — first downtick confirming reversal starting
buy_pe.confirmation: Price ticking down on the first bar after extreme RSI overbought + volume climax

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points (delta ~0.5). If the exhaustion move extends 8 more spot points after entry, the absorption thesis has failed and momentum has resumed. At 30s timeframe, NIFTY typical move is 2-5 option pts; a stop at 4 pts gives the trade two full adverse bars before cutting — consistent with a reversal that should begin immediately.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option points = ~12 NIFTY spot points. Mean reversion from a volume exhaustion spike typically recovers 15-20 spot points in the first 60-90 seconds; targeting 12 pts captures ~70% of the expected recovery at 1:1.5 R:R. Calibrated against the 1-minute typical option move of 3-7 pts.

filters.vix_filter: vix_slope_6 > 0 — slope-based, not level-based; confirms active panic expansion
filters.time_filter: 09:25-15:20 IST — skip first 10min volatility, flatten 10min before close
filters.volume_filter: volume > vol_multiplier * SMA(120) — exhaustion climax required
filters.trend_filter: none — mean reversion trades both directions symmetrically
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at close prices

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral, tied to option seller gamma hedging dynamics

adaptation_notes: The original trades top-10 gainers/losers in the Nifty50 stock universe — a cross-sectional equity filter not applicable to index trading. On NIFTY index, the equivalent is the index's own ultra-short momentum extremes. RSI(2) on 1-min → RSI(6) on 5s: preserves the 'last few bars all one direction' quality (30s vs 2min) while being more robust at 5s resolution. Volume baseline compressed from 50-min to 10-min to avoid blending different intraday regimes. VIX filter changed from level (>15) to rising slope — active panic expansion is what matters for the absorption thesis, not persistently elevated VIX. Hold time compressed from 10-30min to 30-120s because index reversals are faster than stock reversals: institutions hedge at the index level, so NIFTY absorbs the panic/euphoria faster than individual stocks.
weaknesses: RSI(6) at 5s can produce false exhaustion signals during strongly trending microstructure — strong trends can keep RSI pinned at extremes for minutes
Volume climax on index futures can be noisy near expiry due to roll activity inflating volume
VIX 5-second data has gaps; missing readings default to 15.0 (neutral) which may miss genuine panic signals
